title: Reverse engineering: history, protocol analysis, and ethical limits

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “Reverse engineering: history, protocol analysis, and ethical limits” correctly?
options: Voltage pushes charge, current measures its flow, and resistance limits that flow.
Wires appear as lines and joined connections as dots.
Reverse engineering observes and documents how an existing device works.
A resistor limits current, divides voltage, and sets a stable input level.
questions.answer: Reverse engineering observes and documents how an existing device works.
questions.explanation: Reverse engineering observes and documents how an existing device works.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “Reverse engineering: history, protocol analysis, and ethical limits” is accurate?
options: Voltage is measured in volts, current in amperes, and resistance in ohms.
In a four-band code, the first two bands are digits, the third is a multiplier, and the last is tolerance.
It can support repair, interoperability, migration, and debugging of equipment you own or are authorized to test.
Recognizing resistor, capacitor, diode, and ground symbols helps explain how a circuit works.
questions.answer: It can support repair, interoperability, migration, and debugging of equipment you own or are authorized to test.
questions.explanation: It can support repair, interoperability, migration, and debugging of equipment you own or are authorized to test.
